Operator:  
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB, Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Today's conference is being recorded.  

I would now like to turn the call over to Jordan Lee, Vice President of Investor Relations.  

Jordan Lee:  
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GCB's Q3 results. With me on the call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Marketing Officer; and other members of our leadership team.  

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.  

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah.  

Sarah Thompson:  
Thank you, Jordan. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. GCB delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.  

Our discussion today will cover our overall financial performance, brand performance and innovation, supply chain and operational efficiency, marketing and promotional activities, and outlook for the remainder of the year.  

I will now turn the call over to Mike to provide more detail on our financial results.  

Mike Chen:  
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. As Sarah mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $3.25 billion, representing a 7% increase compared to the prior year, including 6.2% organic growth versus a flat category according to Nielsen IRI data. Gross margin was 43.2%, up 180 basis points year-over-year, driven by favorable pricing actions, favorable product mix, and productivity gains that more than offset commodity cost inflation. Operating income was $720 million, up 12%, and diluted earnings per share were $1.48, reflecting 9% growth. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.  

Let me provide more color on these results, starting with our key strategic priorities and the progress we're making. At GCB, our CPG powerhouse spanning snacks, beverages, personal care, and household essentials, we've centered our strategy on three core pillars: portfolio premiumization and innovation, digital and supply chain transformation, and sustainability leadership. These efforts are propelling us toward mid-single-digit organic growth for FY24.  

On portfolio premiumization and innovation, we're optimizing our $12.5 billion portfolio by pruning 8% of SKUs in slower-growth legacy items like traditional sugary cereals, which were only 4% of sales last year, and redirecting $250 million in R&D and marketing toward high-margin, health-oriented platforms, similar to Kellogg's RXBAR move or Mondelez's perfect snacks push. This quarter, our VitaGlow functional beverage line, featuring adaptogens and nootropics, reached 22% household penetration in major U.S. chains like Kroger and Target just 90 days post-launch, grabbing 3.2 share points in the $4.2 billion ready-to-drink functional drinks market. Premium products now make up 42% of sales, up from 35% a year ago, contributing 250 basis points to gross margin expansion. In plant-based categories, GreenPeak almond milk alternatives grew 18% year-over-year in Europe, surpassing the 9% category growth per Euromonitor, supported by a 15% all-commodity volume increase to 65% in retailers like Tesco and Carrefour. Our innovation pipeline is robust, with 15 new SKUs launched year-to-date, 75% achieving velocity goals of 10 units per store per week, positioning us for $800 million in additional premium revenue by year-end.  

Moving to digital and supply chain transformation, consumers are adapting to inflation by shopping more efficiently, with e-commerce now at 18% of U.S. CPG sales per Circana, up from pre-pandemic levels. Our digital sales jumped 32% to $450 million, or 14% of total sales, driven by direct-to-consumer platforms and Amazon performance. CrunchCore snacks, for example, boosted Amazon repeat purchases by 45% using personalized recommendations from Adobe Sensei. Technologically, we've deployed SAP S/4HANA in 80% of our 45 global plants, paired with Blue Yonder's AI demand sensing, cutting forecast errors by 28%, stockouts below 2% from 5.5%, and working capital by 12 days. We've localized 60% of North American sourcing to reduce Asia risks and added IBM Food Trust blockchain for 90% of produce traceability, lifting consumer trust by 15 NPS points. Regionally, North America grew 5% in value despite flat volumes and 4% inflation through pricing; EMEA hit 8% organic growth with 25% e-commerce gains in the UK and Germany; APAC shone at 12%, led by 22% growth in China premium skincare like HydraPure, gaining 1.8 points against L'Oréal in the $15 billion mass prestige space per Kantar; and LatAm volumes rebounded 7% with Argentina stabilizing and Brazil beverage penetration up 10%.  

Sustainability leadership is another differentiator, as 72% of consumers prioritize ESG per Deloitte. We cut virgin plastic 25% in packaging, targeting 50% by 2025 ahead of Unilever, with all snack pouches recyclable via TerraCycle. Scope 3 emissions dropped 18% through regenerative agriculture with 150 U.S. farmers, verified by Regenified like General Mills, and 40% renewable energy in plants. This drives revenue: our EverGreen Certified label enables 14% pricing premiums, and B Corp recertification raised brand favorability to 82% versus the category's 76%. These pillars interconnect—digital speeds innovation testing by 30% via Shopify Plus, and sustainability enhances premium appeal. While inflation risks low-end segments, our 55% value share provides a cushion. We're on track for 5-7% FY24 organic growth and 8-10% EPS expansion, excluding FX.  

Shifting to gross margin specifics, which expanded 180 basis points to 43.2%, 50 basis points above guidance. Commodity costs created a 120 basis point headwind from surges in cocoa up 35% due to West African droughts and pests impacting Ivory Coast and Ghana peers like Hershey and Mondelez; palm oil up 18% from Indonesian curbs and biofuels; plus sugar, wheat flour, and PET resin. We contained this via 75% hedging on 2024 cocoa at 15% below spot, saving $45 million, and 20% palm oil shift to RSPO Latin American sources. SAP Ariba AI analytics improved procurement forecasts 25%. North America had milder 80 basis point drag from local wheat milling; emerging markets steeper at 200 basis points due to FX on USD inputs. We anticipate mid-single-digit moderation in Q4 with South American cocoa ramps and inflation clauses in contracts.  

Pricing provided a 250 basis point tailwind from 5-7% increases: 6% on CrunchMax salty snacks, 7% on RTD beverages, 5% on household cleaners. Elasticity held at -2.5 versus category -3.5 per Nielsen, aided by EDLP and GCB Rewards app penetration up 12%. We gained share in 8 of 10 IRI panels, beating P&G in fabric care and Kellogg in cereals. Europe pricing at 4.5% countered private label; dynamic ML pricing from 150,000 POS points lifted margins 150 basis points via promo ROI. Shrinkflation on 15% value tier packs passed sensory tests. FY24 embeds 4% more pricing, monitoring tariffs.  

Mix added 50 basis points from premiumization—Power Brands like VitalGlow organics and PureIndulge protein snacks up 14% organically to 42% of sales. GreenWave plant-based yogurts at 25% margins beat commodity dairy. Holiday baking favored higher-margin items. North America got 80 basis points from 18% e-comm premium skew; EM neutral. Portfolio pruning lapped drags; Margin Accelerator targets 200 basis points by 2025 via formula tweaks like shea for cocoa butter.  

Our supply chain efficiencies and productivity savings were pivotal, generating $185 million year-over-year, or 2.3% of COGS, offsetting 85% of 7.2% raw material inflation. Under Supply Chain 2.0 since 2023, procurement optimization locked multi-year deals with Cargill for corn and BASF for surfactants, cutting 9% blended via volume and engineering—$42 million from RSPO palm shifts. Supplier consolidation to top 250 improved price variance 450 basis points.  

Network and logistics used Manhattan WMS in 28 North American DCs for 99.7% pick accuracy and 22% throughput, cutting freight 15% per case; dedicated fleets hit 91% truckload utilization, saving $68 million. North America inbound down 12% on diesel; EMEA nearshored palm kernel 18%; APAC multimodal offset typhoons. Manufacturing digitized 75% of 120 plants with Siemens Opcenter, dropping downtime 28%, lifting OEE to 88% for $75 million savings. Blue Yonder cut forecast error 35%, inventory to 42 DOS, freeing $320 million cash for our 12% dividend hike. Supply chain costs fell 160 basis points to 24.8% versus industry 27% per NielsenIQ, targeting $200 million FY25 savings with GenAI routes and blockchain cocoa. OTIF hit 96.5%.  

Promotional strategy effectiveness is another standout, with $285 million spend at 14.2% of sales, flat year-over-year but shifted to Precision Promo for 3.8x ROI, up 15% from 3.3x, beating Mondelez 3.2x and P&G 3.5x amid industry 18-20% intensity. Trade promos at 55% or $157 million secured space at Walmart/Kroger/Target; SnackJoy snacks gained 2.2 points in $25 billion U.S. salty category via PromoForge AI simulating 10,000 scenarios with elasticity and weather, payback 4.2 weeks.  

Consumer promos 30% or $85 million excelled digitally; FreshStart Beverages BOGO via Kroger Boost lifted sales 28% versus 14% average, cannibalization 8%, 5.2x ROI from 45 million GCB Rewards users segmenting baskets up 18%. Experiential 15% or $43 million drove CleanWave 22% volume at Walmart back-to-school, 1.5 points from Unilever; Europe ACV +3 points at Tesco. North America 4.1x ROI via Walmart Connect $25 million incremental at 6:1; LatAm 2.9x mitigated by Mercado Pago 25% redemptions; APAC 4.7x with China Singles' Day $18 million via KOLs, India quick-commerce 40% faster. Shopper Genome NLP forecasts ZIP lifts, cutting waste 22%; dynamic pricing avoids promo traps. Imperatives: trim EDLP 8% protecting margins like Colgate; omnichannel geofencing +15%; eco promos +12% Gen Z repeats. Contributed 42% to 7% organic growth, +110 bps op margins to 22.4%.  

Finally, on competitive activity and responses, the landscape is fierce with 2.1% category growth per NielsenIQ. PepsiCo upped Frito-Lay trade 12% for 4-6 point velocity on Doritos/Lay's EDLP/BOGO, costing us 110 bps ACV to 92.4% in savory snacks. Coke Zero took 2.3 points in CSD with $500 million sustainable PET media. Europe Unilever Dove squeezed personal care at 22% promo depth versus our 18%, 1.8 point loss with 28% private label; EM locals like Parle/Emami sachets hit volumes despite pricing. P&G Tide bio-enzymes +7% repeats, 1.5 points in cleaners; Mondelez Clif 11% in protein bars.  

Our counters: 3.5x ROI trade reallocation $150 million to hero SKUs; CrunchCore Flavor Forward heat variants +450 bps Nielsen share, 1,200 end-caps. Hydrate Smart low-sugar electrolytes +2.1 points in $12 billion functional hydration, 4% soda hikes offsetting volumes, premium +15% to $450 million. Europe Clean Label Garnier Ultra exclusives +80 bps ACV; LatAm Mexico 10g sachets +6% volumes. SymphonyAI planograms +18% efficiency, -22% OOS; 65% recycled packaging matches P&G. Pillars: prune divest $200 million for plant-based M&A; omnichannel DTC/Amazon 12% revenue +40%; elasticity modeling held GM 42.1% vs 300 bps inflation. Expect Q4 intensity but 1-2 point FY24 share gains, $250 million savings EPS boost.  

These elements underscore our Q3 strength and position us for continued momentum. I'll now turn the call over to Lisa to discuss brand performance and marketing.  

Lisa Patel:  
Thank you, Mike. We saw strong performance in our CrunchCore and VitaGlow brands this quarter. Our recent marketing campaigns, including the Flavor Forward campaign, have resonated deeply with consumers, driving velocity and share gains. We're also excited about the launch of our new Hydrate Smart product, a reformulated electrolyte water with less sugar and adaptogens, which is already generating positive feedback and capturing share in the fast-growing functional hydration space. This innovation, combined with targeted digital and in-store executions, contributed significantly to premium mix expansion and overall brand health.  

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.  

Operator:  
Thank you. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with JPMorgan.  

Emily Carter:  
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the details of the new marketing campaign and its impact on sales?  

Lisa Patel:  
Good morning, Emily. Absolutely. The Flavor Forward campaign for CrunchCore focused on bold, heat-infused variants, backed by deeper funding on displays and our PromoForge AI for optimal timing and depth. It delivered 450 basis points of Nielsen share in U.S. salty snacks, with 8% category velocity lift in test markets like Kroger and Walmart, securing 1,200 end-cap placements. Paired with consumer tactics like app-based personalization via GCB Rewards, it boosted basket sizes 18% and hit 5.2x ROI. Overall, promotions including this drove 42% of our organic growth while preserving margins.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from David Kim with Barclays.  

David Kim:  
Thanks. What are your plans for addressing rising commodity costs in the coming quarters?  

Mike Chen:  
Hi David. We're tackling this head-on through hedging—75% of 2024 cocoa locked below spot for $45 million savings—diversification like 20% RSPO palm to Latin America, and AI procurement via SAP Ariba for 25% better forecasts. Supply chain savings of $185 million offset 85% of 7.2% inflation, with procurement cuts of 9%, logistics 15% freight, and manufacturing OEE to 88%. FY25 targets $200 million more, including GenAI and blockchain. Q4 sees moderation, but clauses protect us.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Rachel Lopez with Morgan Stanley.  

Rachel Lopez:  
How is the current inflationary environment impacting consumer demand for your premium product lines?  

Sarah Thompson:  
Thanks, Rachel. Inflation is testing value segments, but our premium lines are resilient, now 42% of sales up from 35%, driving 250 basis points margin expansion. VitaGlow hit 22% penetration quickly, GreenPeak 18% growth in Europe outpacing category. Sustainability like EverGreen boosts 14% pricing power, B Corp favorability 82%. Digital 32% surge to 14% sales buffers via DTC/Amazon. Our 55% value share cushions, guiding 5-7% organic FY24.  

Operator:  
Our next question comes from Tom Nguyen with Citi.  

Tom Nguyen:  
Can you discuss the performance of your e-commerce channel this quarter?  

Lisa Patel:  
Hi Tom. E-commerce was a bright spot, up 32% to $450 million or 14% of sales. CrunchCore Amazon repeats +45% via Adobe Sensei; overall DTC and platforms led, with APAC Singles' Day $18 million burst. Omnichannel synergy—geofenced promos +15% in-store lift—Shopper Genome optimizes at ZIP level. Now 18% U.S. CPG per Circana, our velocity positions us well versus peers.  

Operator:  
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Sarah for closing remarks.  

Sarah Thompson:  
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your questions and participation in today's call. We're confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders, with FY24 organic growth of 5-7%, EPS up 8-10%, and gross margins at 42.5-43.5%. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.  

Jordan Lee:  
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the GCB Q3 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
